meta.description: Build publication-quality figures with matplotlib using the object-oriented Figure/Axes API, constrained_layout, rcParams customization, TrueType (Type-42) font embedding for journal submission, and CVD-safe palettes; covers seaborn integration, common chart types, axis formatting and saving.
meta.execution_note: Every SKILL.md python block was extracted and exec-ed verbatim (run/blocks.py) and the shipped example ran from a scratch copy; matplotlib 3.11.2, seaborn 0.13.2, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.6, Python 3.12.13 (env data-visualization, py.sh). Data is synthetic and labelled so in every script.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated results. The example labels axes 'PC1 (45.2%)' over random stand-in data and says the data are illustrative; flagged as P1, not fabrication

practice_boundaries.detail: Plotting Skill; no clinical or individual-level advice

methodological_ground.detail: No statistical claims; symmetric diverging limits and rasterization guidance verified. The list-palette order pitfall is a defect but the legend is drawn from the same mapping, so no conclusion is inverted

code_usability.detail: Shipped example ran (5 PDFs written, fonts and text verified). Fragments fail on 3 lines on the installed matplotlib or need undefined names (boxplot labels=, Figure.set_rasterization_zorder, tick label count); flagged P1/P2; syntax parses, imports exist

functional_suitability.note: Covers setup, figure/axes, chart types, seaborn, axes, colour, saving. Several verified factual errors: constrained_layout default claim, Figure.set_rasterization_zorder, boxplot labels= (removed in 3.11), list-palette order, editable-SVG claim, 89 mm not met with the Skill's own rcParams

reliability.note: Version-mismatch handling is one generic sentence; fragments fail with NameError/TypeError/ValueError and nothing tells the agent which variables a fragment expects

performance_context.note: 299-line SKILL.md plus a short usage guide; some duplication between SKILL.md, usage-guide and the example; no references/ needed

agent_usability.note: Clear three-defaults framing and a failure-modes section, but 180 mm vs 183 mm double column, prose claims that are wrong (see functional), and snippets that are not self-contained

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language (publication figures, Nature, RNA-seq scatter); tolerant of variants but assumes the caller supplies data names

security.note: No credentials, network or destructive calls; writes only figure files to cwd

maintainability.note: Single-purpose files, runnable example (ran 7/7 sections on matplotlib 3.11.2 / pandas 3.0.6); the example asserts nothing and hides its stand-in data assumptions

agent_specific.note: Precise description; no When-Not-To-Use / escape hatch; Related Skills point at existing folders (verified at the commit)

key_strengths: The core recipe works: rcParams block + subplots(constrained_layout=True) + rasterized scatter gave a Type-42 PDF (ArialMT TrueType, 0 Type 3), extractable text, 6/7 pt font sizes and a rasterized point layer, verified on the PDF bytes
Type-3 default, FacetGrid-vs-Axes, figsize-in-inches, mm-to-inch and colorbar shrink/aspect pitfalls are all real and were reproduced

recommendations.title: boxplot(labels=) removed in matplotlib 3.11
recommendations.problem: The Common Chart Types boxplot line raises TypeError on 3.11.2 ('labels' removed; deprecated in 3.9). The Skill advertises 3.8+.
recommendations.root_cause: API drift not tracked; the version line stops at 3.8+.
recommendations.fix: Use tick_labels= (3.9+) and say labels= is for 3.8 only; raise the version floor or show both.

recommendations.title: fig.set_rasterization_zorder does not exist
recommendations.problem: Failure Modes tells the agent to call fig.set_rasterization_zorder(0); it raises AttributeError. It is Axes.set_rasterization_zorder.
recommendations.fix: Write ax.set_rasterization_zorder(0) and show that artists with zorder below the threshold are rasterized.

recommendations.title: False claim: constrained_layout is the default in 3.6+
recommendations.problem: rcParamsDefault['figure.constrained_layout.use'] is False on 3.11.2; without constrained_layout=True no layout engine is applied. An agent trusting the claim would omit it.
recommendations.root_cause: Confusion with availability of the option.
recommendations.fix: State that constrained_layout must be requested (constrained_layout=True or layout='constrained') and remove the default claim.

recommendations.title: List palette maps colours by appearance order, silently
recommendations.problem: palette=['#999999','#0072B2','#D55E00'] with hue values Up/NS/Down painted Up grey and NS blue (figure opened). A volcano plot with upregulated genes grey is wrong while looking finished.
recommendations.root_cause: Skill and example use a list where a category-keyed dict is needed.
recommendations.fix: Use palette={'NS':..., 'Up':..., 'Down':...} and hue_order in block 3, the seaborn.objects snippet and the example; add a check that legend colours match.

recommendations.title: Hard-coded, invented PC variance labels
recommendations.problem: 'PC1 (45%)' / 'PC1 (45.2%)' are typed into the examples over data whose real variance was 34.6% (canonical input) or random. An agent may copy them.
recommendations.fix: Compute from pca.explained_variance_ratio_ in the recipe, or mark the labels as placeholders to replace.

recommendations.title: '89 mm' is not what is saved; seaborn.objects recipe ignores the setup
recommendations.problem: With savefig.bbox=tight the saved page is 89.42 mm (Skill rcParams) or 91.96 mm (example, default pad), over Nature's 89 mm column. The example's so.Plot figure is 162.56 x 121.92 mm with 11-12 pt text and no rasterization.
recommendations.root_cause: bbox tight resizes the figure; so.Plot uses its own theme and size.
recommendations.fix: For exact size use constrained_layout without bbox tight (or set savefig.pad_inches=0 and state the tolerance); for so.Plot add .layout(size=(w,h)) and .theme(mpl.rcParams) then re-check the size.

recommendations.title: Fragments are not self-contained
recommendations.problem: The tick snippet needs np and mismatches 5 ticks with 3 labels (ValueError); the colour block needs data; the heatmap needs vmax defined; the seaborn.objects snippet never renders.
recommendations.fix: Import numpy where used, make tick and label counts agree, define vmax/data or say so, end the objects snippet with .save() or .plot().

recommendations.title: SVG is 'editable' only after svg.fonttype='none'
recommendations.problem: Default svg.fonttype=path: 0 <text> elements in the saved SVG, text is outlines.
recommendations.fix: Add 'svg.fonttype': 'none' to the rcParams block or reword the claim.

recommendations.title: Inconsistent and unsourced journal numbers
recommendations.problem: Double column 180 mm (SKILL.md, example) vs 183 mm (usage-guide); Nature 5-7 pt, PDF-rejection and the "50 MB" for 100k vector points are unsourced (measured 2.0 MB / 12 s vs 0.36 MB / 2 s).
recommendations.fix: Cite each publisher rule or hedge; use measured numbers.

recommendations.title: No guidance for >8 categories or overplotting order
recommendations.problem: Okabe-Ito has 8 colours; seaborn cycles the list for 12 clusters (8 distinct colours, warning only). Marker-gene colouring is drawn in random order.
recommendations.fix: Point to color-palettes for >8 levels; add sort-by-value for continuous colouring.

recommendations.title: Deprecation and warning debt
recommendations.problem: fig.set_constrained_layout emits PendingDeprecationWarning; seaborn 0.13.2 emits Pandas4Warning on pandas 3; the tight_layout + colorbar clipping claim did not reproduce on 3.11.2.
recommendations.fix: Use fig.set_layout_engine('constrained'); note the versions; soften or drop the tight_layout claim.

recommendations.title: No when-not-to-use / hand-off section
recommendations.problem: The Skill does not say to leave R/ggplot users, interactive figures or genome tracks to other Skills.
recommendations.root_cause: Escape hatches only in Related Skills.
recommendations.fix: Add three lines of scope limits.
